lead.title: Liquid AI launches LFM3: six open-weight 2B-class models on one tri-hybrid backbone
lead.summary: Liquid AI released LFM3 on October 27 — text, vision, audio, omni and two decision models all derived from a shared 1.73B-parameter tri-hybrid backbone (gated short convolutions, sliding-window and global attention). The flagship LFM3-1.7B beats LFM2.5-2.6B with 35% fewer parameters, fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit, carries a 256K context window, and posts a dramatic agentic jump (38.42 vs 3.02 on WebArena-Verified). Weights ship in BF16/FP8/NVFP4/GGUF/MLX/ONNX with llama.cpp support already merged, and Ollama v0.40.12 added the family the same day.

top_stories.title: llama.cpp b11946 adds realtime conversation and transcription on /v1/realtime
top_stories.summary: The October 28 llama.cpp release introduces a server-side realtime endpoint for conversation and transcription, with self-contained server-realtime modules and per-slot sampling fixes for concurrent sessions; prebuilt binaries ship for macOS, iOS and other platforms.

top_stories.title: n8n 3.0.0 beta: legacy nodes removed, security defaults tightened, stable due early December
top_stories.summary: The n8n 3.0.0 beta clears out legacy nodes (Function, Item Lists, Cron, legacy OpenAI and AI Agent modes), tightens security defaults and reworks internals. The upgrade is one-way; 2.x gets security fixes for 12 months and 1.x support ends December 31, 2026.

top_stories.title: MAXSUN plans mini PC with Intel Xe3P 'Crescent Island' GPU D-series, up to 480GB memory
top_stories.summary: At the 2026 Intel LOEM Summit, MAXSUN confirmed Turbo, fanless and mini PC versions of the Xe3P-based GPU D-series accelerator (GPU D270, up to 480GB LPDDR5X), targeting edge AI inference alongside planned workstation and server variants.

items.title: DCKV: a learned transform codec for the prompt KV cache in hybrid language models
items.summary: Presents the first KV-cache codec targeting the prompt state that must be stored or moved for reuse, directly cutting KV-cache memory and bandwidth for local inference with cached prompts.

items.title: CoS-VQ: coordinated shared-scale vector quantization keeps low-bit LLM decoding simple
items.summary: A low-bit weight VQ method that avoids inflating the effective coding dimension, keeping independent codeword lookup and local codeword updates simple for quantized local deployment.

items.title: Channel selection for MoE decoding needs no calibration data
items.summary: Shows channel selectors for routed-expert weights can predict which intermediate channels matter without any calibration data, cutting memory reads in small-batch interactive decoding — the main MoE bottleneck on local hardware.

items.title: CrossInfer shares KV state across CPU/GPU/NPU engines on edge SoCs
items.summary: A joint Wisconsin/Meta/CMU paper separates versioned stream context from per-engine KV state so heterogeneous engines can jointly run stateful VLM inference; on two RK3588 video streams it delivers 19.6% more throughput than the best single engine and cuts first-token latency 4.6x with cross-engine KV import.

items.title: Baidu open-sources Unlimited-OCR 2: a 3B model that parses hundred-page documents in one request
items.summary: Unlimited-OCR 2 uses SR-SWA sparse-reference attention to keep per-step decoding cost nearly flat, so books and filings of hundreds of pages parse in a single request. MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face, code on GitHub, plus a hosted public beta.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash weights go public: 428B MoE for local coding and agentic work
items.summary: The official checkpoint (428B total / 23B active, native multimodal MoE with sparse attention, QAT and a DSpark draft head) is now downloadable ungated at ~252 GB across 48 shards, with GGUF and quant ecosystem builds starting to appear.

items.title: Community ships DSpark draft head for GLM-5.3 for faster local speculative decoding
items.summary: An October 27 upload adds a 6-layer DSpark speculative-decoding draft head for zai-org/GLM-5.3 — block size 16, sliding-window attention, Markov head (rank 256) plus confidence head — a practical speedup lever for anyone serving the 1.5TB-class model locally.

items.title: Survival LLM: an offline AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
items.summary: A fully local AI assistant paired with an emergency reference library, designed to run entirely on the user's hardware with no cloud dependency; the October 27 Hacker News post drew 269 points.

items.title: PVisor runs AI-agent workloads inside VM-isolated containers
items.summary: An open-source tool from DeepLink-org that adds a hardware-virtualization sandbox layer for executing agent-generated code locally.

items.title: Apple launches 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6: 30% faster GPU, 25% faster AI, from $1,999
items.summary: Apple refreshed the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the 2nm M6 chip (12 CPU cores, 12 GPU cores, ~170 GB/s unified memory bandwidth), claiming up to 30% faster graphics and 25% faster AI versus the M5 model, plus Wi-Fi 7 and up to 24-hour battery.

items.title: NVIDIA brings DLSS 5, RTX Kit and on-device Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B to RTX Spark laptops
items.summary: NVIDIA's developer blog details RTX Spark support for DLSS 5 and eight RTX Kit SDKs, and introduces Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB — a small language model built to run in-game AI characters locally on GeForce RTX and RTX Spark while leaving memory headroom for rendering.
